title: Certificates of Deposit: which certificates can take a maximum in-term add-on
content:
## Scope

When the owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate asks to move as much as the certificate will take into it as an in-term add-on, this rule decides whether the certificate can take an in-term add-on at all.

## Rule

A term add-on is allowed only when all three of the following hold:

1. **Status.** The certificate's status is Active.
2. **Opening deposit posted.** The certificate's opening deposit has already posted to it, that is, at least one opening deposit entry stands on its ledger.
3. **Tier.** The tier's most add-ons per term is above zero.

## Checklist with the reading for each item

| Item | Read from | Passes when |
|---|---|---|
| Status | The certificate record | Active |
| Opening deposit | The certificate's ledger | At least one opening deposit entry |
| Tier | The tier's add-on settings | Most add-ons per term above zero |

## Cases (hypothetical certificates)

| Certificate | Status | Opening deposit posted | Tier allows add-ons | Can take an in-term add-on? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Active | Yes | Yes | Yes, as far as this rule goes |
| B | Grace period | Yes | Yes | No, the status is not Active |
| C | Applied | No | Yes | No, the opening deposit has not posted and the status is not Active |
| D | Active | Yes | No | No, the tier takes no in-term add-ons |

## Points of judgement

**The certificate matured and is in its grace period. Can the owner make an in-term add-on now?**
Not while it is in grace period status: an in-term add-on requires the status Active.

**A certificate was opened yesterday and the opening transfer is still on its way. Can an add-on be taken first?**
No. The certificate's opening deposit must already have posted.
